Source claims: section 10 concerns the action of normalisation morphisms of MD-graphs. It seeks maps of the two displayed forms in addition to SΠf for générisation f and Πf for isomorphism f. It says the intersection of the two notions of morphism is isomorphism of MD-graphs. This assertion is transcribed, not proved or verified here.

Source claims: the geometric situation is a stable curve, revised to $X=\widehat X\setminus I$, over an algebraically closed field with letter h|k, with I′⊂I among the points at infinity and A′⊂A among the double points. The sentence ends with a comma; nothing is supplied after it.

Local mathematical cross-reading only: both arrows are plain right arrows; the target I′ of the second map and its adjacent subset condition carry the same visible prime, and this primed subset notation recurs below. This comparison did not decide the overdrawn source I. No theorem, proof or computation was checked; check_events is empty.

The second-map superscript is transcribed as a literal question-mark-shaped sign. The page does not explain whether it is notation or the author’s own hesitation. It is not replaced by a natural sign or exclamation mark.

The geometric replacement contains a visible short backslash. Both cancelled groups are retained, with local doubts under overlapping strikes. The first group is also an insertion attached before SΠf. The lower replacement is attached before sur un corps and is not a separate appended assertion.
The body word meets the right source boundary. The blind adjudication retains normalis followed by doubtful at and omits the absent remainder; the heading does not supply missing strokes.

Neither occurrence of ens has a separate stop; both witnesses supply one. C also supplies a heading-final stop after graphes. The stop after alg. and the stop after the second map’s condition are visible and retained.

H’s editorial folio and title notes are not source prose. Its uncertain entre autres is visually confirmed with the same words, a certainty-only result. Its omitted lower folio and omitted cancelled et are recorded separately.

The unresolved I/overline I and h/k do not charge H with a definite reading error: H’s alternatives remain possible, so both error flags are false for those rows. The connective’s preferred candidate changes from C et to etc at medium confidence while et remains possible. H’s detached stop is not present.
